about: Sections of an essay on romance by Joel (first person). In each, the sentences listed under "changed" were just rewritten; the rest is the essay as it stands. Read each section as it stands, with its heading.

texts.heading: Can Casual Sex or a Situationship Actually Be Honest?
changed: If this girl gets pregnant, she’s gonna call you, and then what?
You block her, or you agree to child support?
sentences: Your body doesn’t know that you picked someone up at a bar and agreed it was only for fun.
Then the next morning, you’re wondering why they didn’t call.
Well, not getting pulled in any further is the best outcome still available, actually, since you just played Russian Roulette with a potential life bond to a stranger.
“I don’t know whether I want something serious with you.
I’m not pretending I do.
I’d still like to have sex.”
That’s honest about what you want tonight, but don't forget that tonight is enough time to make a baby.
If this girl gets pregnant, she’s gonna call you, and then what?
You block her, or you agree to child support?
Try to convince her to abort if she thinks abortion is killing her child?
My first girlfriend, a diehard Baptist, aborted our child and told me a year later, because she “didn’t want to trap” me.
I'm still shocked and saddened about that, 20 years later (assuming it was true).
This is what penetrative sex can do.
No contraception is perfect.
The STI part is easy: say what you know, or say you don’t know.
Feelings aren’t as easy, unless you’re both really numb or robotic about sex.
You have to care what happens to the person afterward.
Otherwise you’re using and abusing them for pleasure.
Maybe they’re using you too.
Congratulations, now it’s mutual.
A lot of “I only want fun” really means, “This is the only version of the relationship that gets me laid.”
Sometimes I know I’m hoping it turns into love.
Sometimes I only find out I was hoping that when it doesn’t.

texts.heading: Dating App Horror Show
changed: I always tell young guys especially: don’t worry about not finding a girl, since finding the wrong one is what should scare you.
Some were cute but none seemed deep, so used as a gate, the app did tell me something useful.
sentences: Ok wait, Judge not, lest ye be judged...
An app could be fine as an introduction if you use it as a proper gate.
Assume 99.99% of the people there are a bad match for you.
If you’re just going to get excited by every cute guy or girl who hits you up, forget it.
That’s such an easy way to find a weirdo, a psycho, a mooch, a faker, or whatever.
Those people are easy enough to find in modern society in person anyway.
I always tell young guys especially: don’t worry about not finding a girl, since finding the wrong one is what should scare you.
Girls are usually more selective, but they still need to think twice, because they often go for guys who aren’t respectful or mature.
I’m almost embarrassed to admit, but I recently tried Hinge again for a few days while I was in Kenya after my last breakup.
I was getting something like a hundred girls interested in my profile every day, so I looked through a lot of profiles.
Some were cute but none seemed deep, so used as a gate, the app did tell me something useful.

texts.heading: Beware idealization in either direction
changed: You can legitimately see someone as amazing when you don’t need anything back from seeing them that way, but you’re already lost in the sauce once you start identifying with the way you see them, like she’s perfect and I’m the one destiny finally sent to find her.
sentences: Idealization can be pathological, but it can also come very close to real deep love and appreciation.
That’s why it’s so easy to get confused.
So far in my life the main experiences of this have been with Bee and Key.
They’re also the two women I’ve actually been in love with, which is probably not a coincidence.
Both of them saw me as their knight in shining armor, and that brought out this divine-feminine beauty in them that made me into a real love slave.
I’m not Superman out here trying to “save a hoe.”
There’s just a natural director/muse dynamic that sometimes plays out in an exaggerated way.
She shouldn’t need a knight in shining armor to bring that beauty out, though, because it’s a bad shortcut to the divine archetypes.

You can legitimately see someone as amazing when you don’t need anything back from seeing them that way, but you’re already lost in the sauce once you start identifying with the way you see them, like she’s perfect and I’m the one destiny finally sent to find her.
The degree of idealization also predicts the degree of demonization for me, so much that I use it almost like a clinical diagnosis in my own life.
If a woman says, “You’re such a great guy.
Of course you have flaws like anyone, but I love you,” that sounds healthy.
If she says, “You’re perfect, I can’t find any flaw,” I’m already running.

texts.heading: The Relationship As Crucible
changed: His idea of differentiation was learning to hold onto yourself while staying close, especially when intimacy brings anxiety and unresolved problems to the surface, which is definitely what relationship has done to me.
If you’re scared to say no or tell the truth, or of what happens if you leave, that’s way past a mutual communication exercise, so get other people involved and think about safety first.
I understand what he means, because it’s much easier for me to feel spiritually advanced when nobody is close enough to expose the parts of me that aren’t.
sentences: It was during my first marriage that I read about Dr. David Schnarch’s Crucible Approach in Passionate Marriage.
Schnarch saw marriage as a natural “people-growing process.”

His idea of differentiation was learning to hold onto yourself while staying close, especially when intimacy brings anxiety and unresolved problems to the surface, which is definitely what relationship has done to me.
One warning before I romanticize the crucible too much: sometimes (as in my first marriage) this isn’t two wounded people triggering each other but one person terrorizing or controlling the other.
If you’re scared to say no or tell the truth, or of what happens if you leave, that’s way past a mutual communication exercise, so get other people involved and think about safety first.
Toft sees the crucible of his marriage as his main spiritual practice.
He also continues his meditation, yoga, prayer, and church activities, but sees them as secondary.
I understand what he means, because it’s much easier for me to feel spiritually advanced when nobody is close enough to expose the parts of me that aren’t.
Being in a relationship showed me how vulnerable I actually am when I open my heart.
It’s really easy to feel invulnerable and strong when you’re alone, or even just with friends.
Taking off the masks and showing your inner child is a gamble, but it’s required if you want to go deeper in yourself and deeper with another person.

texts.heading: Muses & Directors
changed: One time, Bee said she almost got enlightened, but I came too fast... woops!
sentences: In ordinary life, I sometimes think of the woman as the engine and myself as the steering wheel, and I get motivation from her.
She is the life force.
She brings inspiration, beauty, intuition, creativity, and this feeling that life is worth doing.
I help give it direction and make it operational.
I find the intuitive mind incredibly sexy, because I can’t fully follow it.
During sex, some of the most “womanly” women I’ve loved have gone through psychic experiences, memories that felt like past lives, and things I had no idea how to explain.
One time, Bee said she almost got enlightened, but I came too fast... woops!
Key could sometimes start talking and somehow teleport me outside the galaxy.
I don’t know how else to describe it.
Her voice would become so beautiful that I would shed tears that felt super liberating.
Bee could bring out something similar--she could be talking to me for hours on end, but instead of trying to mute her with the TV remote, I felt I was in a timeless dimension of love.

texts.heading: Two Pillars Don’t Hold The Roof Up
changed: With H., I learned another part of the same dyad problem: not to treat what either of us thought the relationship was as a guarantee of what it would remain, because feelings can and usually do change over time.
Make as much community as you can wherever you are, like going to Meetups together and making deep friendships as a couple.
sentences: I lived all the permutations of this with Bee, except that we never lived in community.
I suspect if we had, we might still be together.
She would not have been capable of demonizing me when everyone already knew both of us and knew I wasn’t a narcissistic abuser.
It would have contained all the insanity.
Baseless accusations only work with friends who only know one side.
Commune friends could also have helped her in ways I couldn’t, because she was projecting onto me, which made me the wrong person to help her see beyond the projection.
And it’s actually natural to be a bit BPD when your entire survival depends on one person, because if they aren’t perfect, and especially if you need a lot of support, how will you survive?
One fairly normal but large flaw in them could make your life really difficult.
We were left alone inside something that needed other people around it, and that’s what’s happening to most people these days.

With H., I learned another part of the same dyad problem: not to treat what either of us thought the relationship was as a guarantee of what it would remain, because feelings can and usually do change over time.
In our case, the relationship continued to naturally deepen while our outside relationships often felt more shallow, so it was natural for the dependency to increase.
She was never into monogamy, but that didn’t stop her from becoming possessive once she found someone really worth keeping.
And then she began demonizing me when I refused to be possessed.
Because we did not have a shared community capable of supporting us, her friends heard her side and affirmed her truth.
So if you don’t have a real community already, what can you do about it practically, right now?
Make as much community as you can wherever you are, like going to Meetups together and making deep friendships as a couple.
Find some shared purpose beyond maintaining the relationship.
Introduce your old friends to your partner and try to mutualize those friendships as much as possible, so they aren’t experienced as slyly antagonistic or partial to one side.
You don’t need to spend all your time together, but two completely separate social worlds will automatically start taking sides when something goes wrong.

texts.heading: Why all of this sounds artificial
changed: By now you’re probably thinking all of this sounds terribly artificial: is anyone actually going to do scheduled check-ins, delayed cohabitation, conversations about hypothetical disasters, imagination exercises, not to mention resisting the heat-of-the-moment stuff and continuing your own reparenting practices when a warm body is available to do some of the soothing?
Well, yeah, it is painfully artificial, because in a healthy communal society, the couple would have access to witnesses, elders, friends, and other emotional outlets and resources.
sentences: By now you’re probably thinking all of this sounds terribly artificial: is anyone actually going to do scheduled check-ins, delayed cohabitation, conversations about hypothetical disasters, imagination exercises, not to mention resisting the heat-of-the-moment stuff and continuing your own reparenting practices when a warm body is available to do some of the soothing?
Well, yeah, it is painfully artificial, because in a healthy communal society, the couple would have access to witnesses, elders, friends, and other emotional outlets and resources.
Most of us these days don’t have that, so we’re trying to recreate consciously and clumsily some of what the wider field would have done without a checklist.
